payload.economic_basis: Strive holds bitcoin and sells asset-management services; its preferred stock funds more bitcoin but ranks ahead of common, so a new $500m SATS issue would add bitcoin and a 15% senior claim at the same time. Common holders gain only if bitcoin earns more than the preferred dividend cost and net bitcoin value per common share rises — that is, bitcoin value less preferred claims, divided by diluted shares; one August 2026 window showed 5.5% holdings growth but only 1.3% bitcoin per diluted share, and current bitcoin price, common share count, the missing weekly report and the source of funds are unknown, so I cannot measure whether $25.635 is a premium or discount.
payload.setup: ASST closed at $25.635 on 2026-10-15, up 3.89% that day and 107.7% over three months, with an 'Up / cooling' pattern after a momentum run. The company had just bought 3,311 bitcoin and had announced, but not completed, a $500m SATS preferred sale, so the next three months depend on bitcoin and the financing, not on the past gain alone.
evidence: The 2026-10-15 market snapshot put ASST at $25.635, up 3.89% on the day and 107.7% over three months, with an 'Up / cooling' pattern.

Strive bought 3,311 bitcoin for about $280m at an average $84,500 from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09, lifting holdings to 32,773 bitcoin ([Benzinga](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62320971/strive-acquires-3-311-bitcoins-average-price-84-500-bitcoin-oct-5-through-oct-9)).

Strive announced a planned IPO of 5 million SATS preferred shares at $100 each to raise $500m at a 15% dividend, ranking behind existing SATA preferred that pays about 13% (variable); the sale is not completed ([Benzinga](https://benzinga.com/news/26/10/62341031/strive-plans-conduct-initial-public-offering-5m-shares-its-15-series-perpetual-sats-preferred-shares)).

forecast.pricing_assessment: The 2026-10-15 price of $25.635 came after a 107.7% three-month gain, so I assume it already pays for the completed bitcoin purchases and a successful SATS sale; that is an assumption, not a measured market expectation. Because common shares and current bitcoin price are unknown, I cannot calculate net bitcoin value per share, but the 15% preferred cost means flat bitcoin would reduce the residual for common.
assumptions: Bitcoin's three-month gain stays below the roughly 3.3–3.8% quarterly cost of the existing and planned preferred stock.
The $500m SATS sale closes and the proceeds buy bitcoin, so the senior claim grows without a matching common buyback.
The asset-management business does not generate enough cash to cover the preferred dividends before 2027-01-15.
forecast.opposing_case: The verified 3,311-bitcoin purchase and a completed $500m SATS sale could raise net bitcoin value per common share if bitcoin rallies above the 15% funding cost, and TD Cowen's $132,750 bitcoin target for 2028 supports that path. A short can also lose if Strive uses proceeds for buybacks or if the 2x ASST fund fuels another flow-driven rally.

calls.hypothesis: ASST is more likely to fall over three months because the planned 15% preferred dividend and the existing SATA claim take value ahead of common, while the 107.7% run has left the price dependent on continued bitcoin gains that are not yet proven.
calls.invalidation: The short call fails if Strive discloses that net bitcoin value per common share rises after the SATS sale, or if it uses the proceeds to buy back common stock.
tail_risks: Bitcoin rallies well above $84,500, lifting the value of the treasury faster than the preferred dividend cost.
The SATS sale is priced with a lower dividend or the proceeds are used for common buybacks, reducing the senior claim or supporting the stock.
A 2x ASST fund or momentum buyers force a short squeeze, lifting the share price without a business change.
evidence_limits: Find current diluted common shares and bitcoin price to calculate net bitcoin value per share after preferred claims, which decides whether $25.635 is a premium or discount.
Find the missing weekly bitcoin purchase report and the source of funds for the 3,311-coin purchase, which shows whether reported accumulation reconciles and who paid for it.
Confirm the final SATS terms, closing date and use of proceeds, because a smaller sale, higher dividend or buyback would change the value left for common.
